newsitem.title: UK: FEATURE - Millennium party tickets selling out fast.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Millennium party tickets selling out fast.

text.p: Walt Disney World in Florida, the Tour d'Argent in Paris and the Seattle Space Needle are sold out and tickets are going fast for other world-famous venues.
The year 2000 is still three years away but luxury hotels, tourist resorts and nightclubs say it is never too early to book for what is billed as the celebration of the century.
"Everybody is going to do something. The world will sell out for the millennium," Skip Kitchen of Millennium Celebrations Inc. told Reuters.

"Virtually every major public venue -- hotels, convention centres, restaurants -- will have some type of celebration. There is a human propensity to gather. People want to celebrate. It is the end of a millennium, a decade, a century. It is a unique time -- a defining moment."
Kitchen's Chicago-based marketing and special events firm, was founded in 1994 specifically to create events tied to the millennium.
The company is co-ordinating a five-day series of special celebrations in cities around the globe and merchandising special millennium products to promote festivities.
TIMES SQUARE PARTY
Times Square in the heart of New York city will commemorate the magic moment with a 24-hour global party tracking the millennium in each of the planet's 24 time zones.

"New Year's Eve is celebrated in different ways around the world. Because of the rich diversity of New York City, we felt it was appropriate to use Times Square as the venue to celebrate the world's culture," said Gretchen Dykstra, president of the Times Square Business Improvement District.
Giant television screens will beam the festivities from such faraway places as Fiji, Iceland and Bangkok, and the traditional lighted ball will also be lowered at the stroke of midnight.
The Times Square party will start at 7 a.m. on December 31st in New York when residents of Fiji usher in the new year on the far side of the globe.

The "Big Idea" was chosen after a year-long search from 640 suggestions submitted from 21 countries. Despite ideas such as a parachuting Jesus, or giving party goers a "happy juice" cocktail of anti-ageing mushrooms and marijuana and requiring them to wear diapers (nappies), organisers chose the video link.
The Empire State Building will also hold a free party but is keeping its plans under wraps until late 1999.
Although the 200 seats costing $1,000 each (minus drinks) in the Rainbow Room restaurant atop Rockerfeller Centre are sold out, 600 people on a waiting list are hoping for cancellations.
EUROPEAN CELEBRATIONS
The European Union, not to be outdone, is planning a major extravaganza involving nine cities -- Avignon, Bergen, Bologna, Brussels, Krakow, Helsinki, Prague, Reykjavik and Santiago de Compostela.
A special committee has been working on political and practical guidelines for the millennium and representatives from the selected cities have met to co-ordinate the festivities.
In London, the Savoy, a stylish Art Deco hotel on the banks of the river Thames, has been fielding questions about its millennium party for the past decade.
"Judging from the inquiries we've received we could have filled the hotel twice over," said spokeswoman Ros Choate.
A committee is deciding how the hotel will mark the event and the lucky guests will be chosen through a ballot system.

Deeper in the English countryside, the Lygon Arms, a five-star, 16th century coaching inn in the Cotwolds is planning a four-day celebration starting on December 30, 1999 that will set back guests 2,000 pounds ($3,295).
But across the English Channel in France, enthusiasm for the millennium is distinctly lacking.

"In Britain, people are fascinated, spellbound. In France, for the time being, people are paying almost no attention whatever," said Richard Geoffroy of the Moet & Chandon champagne house. "I expect a rush of interest here at the very last minute, that's the French way."
Although Paris' posh Tour d'Argent restaurant has been fully booked for the millennium for months, most of the city's other fashionable venues have not announced any special plans.
ASIAN EVENTS
Sydney will be hosting a huge masquerade party and a fireworks show on the city's spectacular harbour.
"We want to show off...Sydney as the first major world city to cross the dateline, especially in the lead-up to the (2000) Olympic Games," said the city's Lord Mayor Frank Sartor.
Revellers will be encouraged to wear masks, the harbour will host a "boat ballet" and five tonnes of fireworks will be shot from 25 locations.

Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese control in six months, has not annnounced its plans but judging from its spectacular New Year's celebrations, its millennium party will be one to remember. ($1=.6069 Pound)
